steps.content: At long last, the tumultuous DisCars crisis is coming to an end, all thanks to you, Deren, and OwO. You take a team of soldiers to search every nook and cranny of Dillywood, in case that formidable force is lying in wait in some dark corner.
The host of the DisCars ceremony has booked five venues for the special occasion. Now, surrounded by a cluster of gigantic buildings, you can't help but heave a sigh.
This is gonna be a long night.
You move your head from side to side to ease the soreness in your neck, and step through the gaping hole created by the Apostle of Ashes to investigate the complex in the back.
Excuse me, coming through...
The moment you step into the alley, you hear a stream of footfalls coming your way.
Then you see a familiar figure approaching you.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: Ah, Chief!
Deren catches her falling hat and strides toward you.
Without saying anything further, she grabs your hand and starts running, dragging you along, much to your surprise.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: What a coincidence! Us meeting again here and now!
Hold on!
What are you doing?
Before you can get an answer, you hear a confusion of voices coming from behind.

steps.speaker: Producer A
steps.content: Miss Deren, please stop running for a minute! Take a look at this new contract. I'm sure you'll be happy with the terms!

steps.speaker: Producer B
steps.content: We'll double whatever they offer you, as long as you sign with us!

steps.speaker: Reporter A
steps.content: Miss Deren, could you tell us why you've decided to attend this ceremony? And is the person running with you the star of your next movie?

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: Sorry! But I can't answer any questions right now!

steps.speaker: Reporter B
steps.content: How about you, mister? Do you have something to say?
steps.female_content: How about you, miss? Do you have something to say?

steps.content: You can't think of anything to say while you're running your heart out.
Right at this moment, you catch sight of a hill of rubble ahead. That's the place where you fought the Apostle of Ashes.
You speed up and get ahead of Deren, pulling her instead. The two of you slip into the dilapidated building.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: (Pants)...
...Care to explain, Miss Big Director?

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: Hehe... I used to be, um, quite famous.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: Well, you know, the DisCars ceremony has been delayed. Those guys are not gonna go home empty-handed... so they have been vying to sign me or get me on interviews.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: They're like bloodhounds. They know exactly where to find me.
Deren puts her hand on the nape of her neck, a look of resignation on her face.

options: I might have a solution to your conundrum.

choices.text: I might have a solution to your conundrum.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: Really? What is it?
Follow me.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: Hey, where are you taking me?
Just follow me. You'll find out.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: This is... your solution?
The MBCC headquarters is a high-security facility. No ordinary folks can get in without permission from me or one of my superiors.
If you agree to be detained and stay here, not only will you be rid of those nuisances, but you will be protected. Two birds with one stone, don't you think?

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: So, simply put, free food and accommodation, right?
...Yeah, you could put it that way.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: Hmm, sounds great.
Deren plunks herself down on the chair in the interrogation room, seemingly at ease. She looks up at you with a smile on her face.
...Aren't you gonna resist a little?

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: Resist? Why would I?

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: I'm a Sinner, and you are the Chief of the MBCC. Me being detained here is a matter of course.
...You have a point.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: Plus, here, I get free food and accommodation. Out there, I have to fend for myself, while hiding from my pursuers.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: It's an easy option. Wouldn't you agree, Chief?
You can't figure out what's going on in the head of this happy-go-lucky Sinner before you. Is she really ignorant of how the relationship between the MBCC and Sinners works, or...
Is she just playing dumb, biding her time?
Once you've decided to stay, it won't be easy to back out.
All Sinners, once detained by the MBCC, must take orders from me, no questions asked.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: Well, I'm aware of that.
Deren narrows her eyes at you. The way she is now speaking reminds you of your first conversation with her, where you had a hard time deciphering her words.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: Taking orders from you, not taking orders from you... Doesn't make much of a difference to me. At least I can live comfortably here.
Surely a famous director like you can easily find a place to live comfortably?

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: Hmm, I need a change of scenery, if you really need an explanation.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: And there is no place in the entire DisCity more special than the MBCC headquarters, where I can "stay close to you".
I don't suppose you want to make a movie about Sinners, do you?

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: That actually sounds like a great idea.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: No one has ever made a movie like that before.
Then what? Submit it to the DisCars and win half a dozen trophies?

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: Oh my, wouldn't that be fantastic.
Deren waggles her eyebrows at your question, or more specifically, at the mention of the DisCars.
You exchange glances and chuckle.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: You said the MBCC headquarters is a high-security facility. Your words, not mine.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: Would anyone understand a movie about an organization that has never dared to show its face in public?

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: Oh... wait a second...
Deren strokes her chin, her face a study in contemplation, as if ready to deliver some devastating news.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: Understand or not, that's not even our first concern. Whether it would be allowed to be released, that would be the real issue.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: Those guys...
Deren tips her head back slightly, signaling you to look at the roof above the two of you.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: They would never allow a movie like that to be screened in the DisCars.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: What else could it be?
Deren starts counting on her fingers while murmuring to herself. After a while, she shows her hands with the palms facing out.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: I can give you ten reasons, at the very least.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: But I won't elaborate on them; I don't want your interrogation report to be rejected.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: Haha... You're so amusing.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: What do you mean, even if it's my movie?

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: It's exactly because it's my movie...

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: They'd be more strict, more unreasonable, in vetting it.
Deren falls silent. Her eyes are shielded from view by the brim of her hat, so you can't see how she is feeling inside.
They put restrictions on your movies, forcing you to make changes to suit their taste... Is that the reason why you loathe them?
You twirl the cap of your fountain pen, pull it out, and put it back on with a click, a sound not unlike that of a clapperboard.
At the sound, Deren lifts her eyes to look at you, shaking her head.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: I don't loathe them.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: I just find them... very boring.
Deren stretches and rests her head on her hand, looking as if she is about to fall asleep.
You didn't use to hate the DisCars so much, did you? You attended a few DisCars ceremonies before you quit directing, if I'm not mistaken.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: Alas, everyone has a living to earn, my dear Chief, even a talented director.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: I have to say I'm not as assertive as I used to be.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: Have you heard that I didn't attend the DisCars ceremony where my award was presented? That's right before I quit directing.
I heard. Nobody held it against you. Quite the opposite, a lot of people thought you had...
Character.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: Character?

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: That's something I do not have.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: It's just a flawed choice made by the immature me.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: As for the audience and judges...
Deren's smiling eyes have narrowed into slits. Their brilliance is mostly trapped behind the heavy eyelids.
She snickers, closing her eyes for a second.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: They only saw what they wanted to see, or what they were tricked into seeing.
Why didn't you attend the ceremony then?
The DisCars are the most prestigious awards in the entertainment industry, right?

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: But the movie they submitted for consideration in my name didn't deserve them.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: Even though the audience, judges, and everyone else thought it did.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: I didn't think so.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: So I didn't attend it, because it was their party. It had nothing to do with me.
Deren sounds breezy. It's as if she doesn't think much of the highly-regarded awards.
I've never seen a director who doesn't want to join the "party" with audiences.
Something went wrong in the production of the movie?

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: How very observant of you!

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: How about I tell you a little story, Mr. Clapper. And then you can tell me what is real, and what is false...
steps.female_content: How about I tell you a little story, Miss Clapper. And then you can tell me what is real, and what is false...

steps.content: Deren narrows her eyes at you again. The smile she gives you is strangely familiar.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: In the open sea drifts a lifeboat, which holds a woman, a tiger, a dog, a monkey, and a hippo.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: Threatened by the mere existence of the tiger, the dog, monkey, and hippo gang up to get rid of the tiger. And when the big cat asks the woman for help, she says,

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: "You have to go so the rest of us can live."

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: But she tells herself, "You have to go, for your own sake."

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: Well, take a guess, which is true? Is it what she says to the tiger, or what she says to herself...

options: What she tells herself is true.
What she tells herself is false.

choices.text: What she tells herself is true.
What she tells herself is false.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: That's what most people would guess.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: Thinking outside the box... I like that.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: But the truth is, it doesn't matter what you believe. It's what you do that matters.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: So... the woman jumps into the sea with the tiger, never to be seen again.
You... I mean, she... disappears with the tiger, but the lifeboat and other animals are intact, right?

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: Correct. The dog, monkey, and hippo, now sure of their safety, start celebrating, like they have received <color=#fb9259>The Invitation to Dance</color>, and it didn't matter if they were dancing of their own free will or if they were forced to.
Are you saying...

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: Yes... it's not all that complicated... The movie submitted for consideration was not the version I edited.
Deren puts it lightly, but you catch on immediately.
Even OwO, a newcomer to the film industry, understands the importance of direct involvement in editing. It's the only way of ensuring your story is accurately presented.
If the task is assigned to someone else, some of the ideas you wish to present will inevitably be missing in the final product.
And if you're unlucky enough, the theatrical version can have an entirely different message than the director's cut.
What kind of message did you want to get across in your version?

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: Mmm...

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: I don't remember.
Deren hangs her head, deep in thought. After a while, she looks up at you and shrugs her shoulders before giving you a non-committal reply.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: It's been changed so drastically that I'm not even sure I could recognize it now.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: I don't understand why people are still so obsessed with a movie that has nothing to do with me.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: Maybe because they are just... bored.
Deren must be lying. She can't have forgotten what the original version of the movie is about...
You muse, as you look at Deren, who has closed her eyes.
Deren seems to have lost interest in continuing this discussion about her movie. You decide to call it a day and end the questioning.
